title: Chapter 19: Nitric Oxide
numbering_note: The syllabus assigns 'Chapter 19' for the 10/1 signal transduction and autonomic nervous system overview, but Katzung 16e Chapter 19 is Nitric Oxide (the autonomic overview is Chapter 6, also in Drive). Recorded as found. The content backs the 10/7 lecture's nitric oxide synthase topic; the signal-transduction half of 10/1 is covered by Chapter 2's 'Signaling Mechanisms & Drug Action'.
about: Nitric oxide (NO) is a gaseous signaling molecule that is generated by specific cells in the body and readily diffuses across cell membranes to regulate a wide range of physiologic and pathophysiologic processes including cardiovascular, inflammatory, and neuronal functions. Nitric oxide should not be confused with nitrous oxide (N2O), an anesthetic gas, or with nitrogen dioxide (NO2), a toxic pulmonary irritant gas. The major target of NO is soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC), a heme-containing enzyme that generates cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) from guanosine triphosphate (GTP).
sections: Discovery of Endogenously Generated Nitric Oxide
Nitric Oxide Synthesis, Signaling Mechanisms, & Inactivation (enzymatic synthesis, signaling via metalloproteins/thiols/tyrosine nitration, inactivation)
Pharmacologic Manipulation of Nitric Oxide (NO donors, augmenting endogenous NO, inhibitors of NO synthesis)
Nitric Oxide in Disease (vascular effects, septic shock, infection & inflammation, CNS, PNS, respiratory disorders)
read_for: Table 19-1 'Properties of the three isoforms of nitric oxide synthase': nNOS (NOS-1), iNOS (NOS-2), eNOS (NOS-3) - tissue, constitutive vs inducible expression, Ca2+/calmodulin vs transcriptional activation (10/7).
'Enzymatic Synthesis' and Figure 19-1: L-arginine + O2 + NADPH -> NO; cofactors heme, tetrahydrobiopterin, FAD; PIEZO1 shear-stress activation of eNOS.
'Signaling Mechanisms' 1 and Figure 19-2: NO -> sGC -> cGMP -> PKG -> reduced Ca2+ -> vasorelaxation; the EDRF story linking acetylcholine/muscarinic endothelial responses to NO.
'Discovery of Endogenously Generated Nitric Oxide': endothelium-dependent vasodilation by acetylcholine (ties to Katzung Figure 7-5 and the 10/6 muscarinic lecture).

'Pharmacologic Manipulation': NO donors as prodrugs (nitroglycerin via ALDH-2, nitroprusside), PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil), sGC stimulators (riociguat, vericiguat), NOS inhibitors (Table 19-3: L-NMMA, L-NAME).
'The Peripheral Nervous System': NO as the NANC transmitter (penile erection) - connects back to the Ch 6 NANC section.
beyond_lecture: S-nitrosylation of thiols, peroxynitrite and tyrosine nitration (Table 19-2 oxidized nitrogen species).
NO in disease: atherogenesis, septic shock and the failure of NOS inhibitors in trials, inflammation (psoriasis, asthma, IBD), CNS excitotoxicity.
Inhaled NO for neonatal hypoxic respiratory failure and pulmonary hypertension; methemoglobin and NO2 monitoring.
Amyl nitrite abuse and the lethal interaction with PDE-5 inhibitors.

terms.chapter_definition: a gaseous signaling molecule that is generated by specific cells in the body and readily diffuses across cell membranes to regulate a wide range of physiologic and pathophysiologic processes.
a soluble factor released by endothelial cells in response to vasorelaxants that diffuses into vascular muscle and causes vasorelaxation; NO is the major bioactive component of EDRF.

neuronal NOS (nNOS or NOS-1), macrophage or inducible NOS (iNOS or NOS-2), and endothelial NOS (eNOS or NOS-3), each encoded by a separate gene and named for the initial cell type from which it was isolated.
the NOS isoforms generate NO from the amino acid L-arginine in an O2- and NADPH-dependent reaction involving enzyme-bound cofactors heme, tetrahydrobiopterin, and FAD.
iNOS is not regulated by calcium, but instead produces NO in proportion to the expression level of iNOS, which is induced by inflammatory mediators.
a heme-containing enzyme that generates cGMP from GTP; NO binds and activates sGC activity several hundredfold.
prodrugs that require biotransformation in order to release NO; they do not spontaneously release NO.
formed when large amounts of both NO and superoxide are produced; a highly reactive and short-lived oxidant that leads to nitration of tyrosine and DNA.
